% {\footnotesize\raggedright
% Percentages over the MMLongBench-Doc answerable pool, page-level against the annotated
% evidence pages. Bold is the best value in each column within a gold-page group.
% \textbf{$k{=}g$ is the operating point a deployment actually has}, because how many pages an
% answer needs is usually known when the question is asked: it is $k{=}1$ in the first group
% and $k{=}2$ in the second. The sweep stored $k \in \{1,3,5,7,10\}$; rankings are strict
% prefixes of one another, so the unswept $k{=}2$ is derived by truncating the $k{=}10$ list.
% \textbf{Precision is capped by construction at $g/k$} --- 100 at $k{=}g$, then 33.3, 20.0,
% 14.3 and 10.0 for a single gold page --- so it falls across a row by arithmetic rather than
% by the retriever getting worse. Recall carries no ceiling and is what compares across depths.
% \textbf{A union arm's $k$ is per constituent}, so it returns up to $2k$ deduplicated pages
% and its precision is divided by what it actually returned; that is the trade the union makes
% and why it sits above its constituents on recall and below them on precision at the same
% nominal depth. The two union arms were stored only to $k{=}5$ and do not nest, so nothing is
% derived for them and $k{=}2$, 7 and 10 are blank.
% \textbf{Vision retrieval dominates the text arm at every depth and both gold counts.}
% ColQwen3 reaches 74.0 recall at $k{=}g$ on single-page questions against BM25's 29.6, and
% still leads at $k{=}10$ (93.3 against 65.6). Questions citing three or more gold pages are
% not shown: 112 questions spread over counts up to 24 is too thin to split per count and too
% heterogeneous to pool. \textbf{The gap is not an artifact of a weak text arm.}
% \emph{Qwen3-Embedding} is the strongest text retriever at every fixed depth --- 69.4 recall at
% $k{=}10$ on single-page questions against BGE-M3's 65.4 and BM25's 65.6 --- and still trails
% ColQwen3 by 23.9 points there, so replacing the text retriever does not close the distance to
% page images.\par}
